newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end down despite good profit data.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end down despite good profit data.

text.p: Austrian shares fell 0.65 percent in slow trade on Wednesday, continuing a retracement towards 1,080 points that was triggered by the market's failure to break above 1,100 at the start of the week.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares closed 7.12 points down at 1,081.48 despite a rise in earnings at blue-chip firms Mayr-Melnhof and Radex-Heraklith.
"Not even these positive figures could jolt the market awake," said a trader.
Most market participants took the decline in their stride, however, arguing that downside was limited.
"The 1,080 level will certainly hold," one said.
The day's biggest decliner was semi-conductor maker AMS, which took a battering after German software group SAP shaved its earnings estimates.
AMS was already suffering ahead of the release of its third quarter results next week. AMS has delayed the data by one day to October 31.
"Some investors are bailing out ahead of the results, which most people assume will be bad," said a trader.
AMS dipped 5.01 percent, or 41 schillings, to 777 schillings.
Building materials firm Wienerberger and national utility Verbund will release their nine-month profit figures on Thursday and Friday respectively.

Overall four ATX shares closed up and 17 down. November ATX futures stood 7.6 points down at 1,084. The broad-based Vienna bourse index ended 2.8 points down at 414.79. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
